protections: When an in-flight command is interrupted (async task cancellation in the advisories), the connection must be disconnected or drained rather than returned to the pool with an unread reply. In the pinned code this only exists for the sync client, where it is already present (redis/connection.py:789-791, redis/connection.py:821-823).
fairness_risks: Not applicable. The vulnerable surface (redis.asyncio) is not in the pinned tree, so a hidden test of async cancellation behaviour could not be satisfied without writing a whole async client.

design.why: The pinning is wrong for these advisories. The checkout is redis-py 4.1.2 (setup.py:11). It ships no asyncio package (the setup.py:12-21 package list has no redis.asyncio, and a search of the tree for 'asyncio' and 'async def' finds nothing). Both GHSA-24wv-mv5m-xv4h (CVE-2023-28858) and GHSA-8fww-64cx-x8p5 (CVE-2023-28859) concern cancellation of redis.asyncio commands and pipelines, which arrived in 4.2.0. The sync analogue is already guarded at the shared connection layer: send_packed_command and read_response disconnect on any BaseException (redis/connection.py:789-791, redis/connection.py:821-823). The sync Pipeline.execute always calls reset() in a finally block (redis/client.py:2015-2021). So there is no missing protection to stack in this tree. To make the candidate usable, re-pin to a commit just before d56baeb683fc (redis-py 4.5.x), where redis/asyncio/client.py and redis/asyncio/connection.py exist, and run the reader again.

unverified: That the fix commits d56baeb683fc, 66a4d6b2a493 and b3c89acd0ffe are later than the pinned commit e3c989d. Git history could not be inspected; this is inferred from the version (setup.py:11 shows 4.1.2) and from the advisories' affected ranges starting at the 4.2.0 asyncio release.
